chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Her uncle's Homestead band
summary: An integrated brass band with an uncle who played tenor sax and many instruments.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: and forth, you know. But I stayed with Aunt Jo. MR. HUGHES: If your father hadn't died, you would not have spent as much time with -- MS. SULLIVAN: I probably would have because the families were very close. Yeah, there was no problem there. I guess I stayed with Aunt Jo until I got old enough to go to public school and then of course I came back to Homestead and I was staying with my mother and my grandmother. So I went to school in Homestead, not particularly concerned about a career at that early stage but I think my grandmother, my father's mother was very well known in Homestead and family so at every opportunity at concerts, I was always on stage doing something. I remember singing, 'I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles' in 1918 on the stage at the Carnegie Library in Homestead. But that was just part of, you know, being part of that family.
You sang that to the accompaniment of your uncle --
I'm not sure who. I might have sung it without any accompaniment. Harry

wasn't around at that time. One of my aunts, the one I was named after, we called her Aunt May, she was married to a musician who was the leader of the local Homestead band. And so therefore they did quite a few concerts and I was always --
When you say the Homestead band, you mean a brass band, like a marching band.

Yes. Well, he played tenor sax himself and he played all the instruments but when he appeared with the band he would play saxophone. The Homestead band participated in the parades and they also did concerts. They also played at dances, too, for the local gentry. And as I recall I was always on stage;and they would present fashion shows, church concerts and I was always doing something.
Yes, it was an integrated band. Well, all the musicians, you know, who wanted to be in it would be in it. It was actually the Homestead
